🔥🇲🇽 <u>AMLO Returns: Fobaproa Will Cost Mexico 8.4 Trillion Pesos</u>

Reappearing in a video message to present his new book "Pueblo," López Obrador put a final price on Zedillo's bank bailout: 8.4 trillion pesos by the time it's paid off, "until 2050, if things go well." So far 1.6 trillion pesos have gone to interest alone, and the principal hasn't moved.

He reminded viewers who brokered it: the PRI and the PAN, with Felipe Calderón negotiating for Acción Nacional. He also noted that under Calderón and Peña Nieto, 50 big corporations got 300 billion pesos in tax forgiveness. That ended with his constitutional reform to Article 28.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Pemex Crude Exports Plunge 44.8% as Mexico Refines at Home</u>

Pemex shipped just 275,737 barrels a day of crude abroad in August, down 44.8% from a year earlier and 39% from July, according to La Jornada. Revenue from foreign crude sales fell 34.3% to $626.9 million.

The barrels aren't vanishing. They're going into Mexican refineries, which raised gasoline and diesel output the same month. For decades Mexico sold crude cheap and bought back fuel dear. That trade is now being reversed.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum to Washington: Revoke Asylum for the Ayotzinapa Judge</u>

President Sheinbaum is demanding the US withdraw asylum from José Ulises Bernabé García, the on-duty Iguala barandilla judge the night 43 Ayotzinapa students were disappeared in 2014. He fled north in 2015, claimed "persecution," and the US Justice Department granted him protection in 2020 — while Mexico seeks his extradition.

Mexico has handed Washington dozens of cartel figures it wanted. Sheinbaum's demand is reciprocity: "You cannot be asking on one side and not responding on the other."

🇲🇽🌾 <u>Michoacán wheat: 7,600 pesos a ton vs 4,600 on the market</u>

Federal guaranteed prices for small and medium producers in Michoacán run from 7,050 to 9,080 pesos per ton (El Economista). Small wheat farmers get 7,600 pesos, plus a 200-peso climate incentive, against an average rural price of about 4,600. Small rice growers get 9,080 against about 5,800. That's roughly 3,000 extra pesos a ton for the smallest wheat farms, across 27,284 hectares in 54 municipalities.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico and Canada deepen intelligence and cybersecurity ties</u>

Security chief Omar García Harfuch met the Business Council of Canada, led by Goldy Hyder, and announced broader binational cooperation on intelligence and cybersecurity, where information-sharing is key. The Canadian side acknowledged the results of Sheinbaum's security strategy and the SSPC's work strengthening intelligence and investigation.

🇲🇽🌽 <u>Oaxaca maize defenders: "We don't sow maize to sell"</u>

On National Maize Day, Oaxaca's Espacio Estatal en Defensa del Maíz Nativo accused federal farm policy of still shielding transnational industrial agriculture while maize has become one of Mexico's biggest imports. They demand that RNA biopesticides never be produced or used in the country and call on farmers to keep swapping native seeds through guelaguetza and mano vuelta, without money: "We don't sow maize to sell."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>"The spurious Calderón talking about democracy"</u>

Felipe Calderón, who took office in 2006 by a 0.56-point margin under fraud allegations that never went away, is a headline guest at América Libre, a right-wing forum in Mexico City gathering activists from 25 countries and sponsored by, among others, Calderón himself and the PAN. Sheinbaum: "If he talks about democracy, my goodness, it would be a jewel. The spurious Calderón talking about democracy. That's how the Mexican right is." She still wished him "maximum freedom of expression."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Interpol drops red notice on Mexico's "invoice fraudsters"</u>

Interpol quietly withdrew its red notices on Inés Gómez Mont and Víctor Manuel Álvarez Puga, wanted in Mexico since 2021 for organized crime and money laundering tied to a fake-invoice tax-evasion network. Sheinbaum: "They are two recognized invoice fraudsters, with arrest warrants in Mexico, with all the evidence that they were dedicated to issuing false invoices to evade taxes." Mexico is demanding Interpol's reasons and asking for the notices to be reinstated.

🇲🇽📈 <u>Mexican Pension Funds Hold a Record 4.3 Trillion Pesos in Government Bonds</u>

Per El Financiero, Mexico's Afores held a record 4.3 trillion pesos ($241 billion) in local peso government debt in August, according to Banxico data. That is up 6% this year and 32% since the start of 2025. When foreign investors pulled more than $1 billion out of Mexican bonds in March, workers' savings stayed put. "They don't sell. They hold their positions," said VanEck's Natalia Gurushina. Fitch says Mexico is "well positioned to meet almost all its financing needs in the domestic market."
banner: AFORES: RECORD 4.3T PESOS IN GOV'T BONDS

🇲🇽🚆 <u>Valley of Mexico Gets Its First New Metropolitan Plan Since 1998</u>

Mexico City, the State of Mexico, Hidalgo and Morelos, together with the federal urban development ministry Sedatu, are updating the Valley of Mexico metropolitan zoning program for the first time since 1998. The plan covers transport, water supply, drainage and protected green areas across 84 municipalities and boroughs, a region of about 22.7 million people. Public consultation is open until November 22.
